newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks up 1.85 pct by lunch break.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks up 1.85 pct by lunch break.

text.p: Thai stocks advanced 1.85 percent in active morning trade on Thursday as foreign investors speculated in favour of large bank and finance companies, brokers said.
"Foreigners focus their buying on blue-chip bank and finance stocks this morning," said Padermpob Songkroh of Nava Finance and Securities.
The composite SET index rose 11.73 points to 647.44 on moderate 4.3 billion baht turnover by lunch.
Five finance firms selected by the central bank to head corporate mergers in the sector, including Krungthai Thanakit, Dhana Siam, National Finance, Phatra Thanakit and Nava Finance, rallied sharply.
Sixteen suspended finance firms have been instructed by the central bank to produce merger plans by Friday or they would be forced to merge with the five finance firms.
Nava Finance gained 1.50 baht to 17.25, Dhana Siam rose 2.25 to 25.25, National Finance surged 2.50 to 27.75, Phatra advanced 3.75 to 42.75, and Krungthai was up 2.25 to 26.
Most key sectors gained by the lunch break.
The banking sector was the most active in the morning, rising 2.23 percent, followed by the finance counter which gained 5.66 percent, and the communication sector which advanced 5.18 percent.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, gaining 0.75 baht to 35.50.
